CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to assess the management of anxiety, sleep disturbances, persistent fatigue, and headache symptoms.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his scheduled follow-up appointment, expressing mixed feelings regarding his treatment progress. He reports a marginal improvement in sleep quality, noting that he has been able to achieve approximately 7.5 hours of sleep per night. However, he continues to struggle with sleep initiation and frequent nocturnal awakenings, which he describes as emotionally taxing. He has been compliant with his medications, including sertraline 200 mg daily and trazodone 50 mg nightly, yet remains interested in exploring alternative options to further enhance his sleep quality.
Despite the slight improvement in sleep duration, Mr. Smith reports that his fatigue remains a significant issue, particularly during workdays. He attributes this ongoing fatigue to both persistent sleep disturbances and the stress associated with looming project deadlines at work. He indicates that his headache frequency has remained stable at four times per week, with intensity fluctuating between 3 and 7 on a scale of 10. He has continued to take amitriptyline at 30 mg nightly, but he feels that the relief from headaches is inadequate. He occasionally resorts to ibuprofen 400 mg, which provides minimal relief.
Mr. Smith has maintained his acupuncture sessions twice weekly, which he finds beneficial. He continues his yoga practice and has been diligent in implementing relaxation techniques and mindfulness strategies, reporting that these have been moderately effective in managing his anxiety, although he still grapples with significant work-related stress.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 200 mg daily 2. Trazodone 50 mg at bedtime 3. Melatonin 10 mg at bedtime 4. Lisinopril 10 mg daily 5. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief 6. Amitriptyline 30 mg nightly 7. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (usage stable)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to work as a software engineer, where project deadlines are a significant source of stress. He remains committed to physical activity, regularly attending yoga classes and incorporating meditation practices into his routine. He abstains from alcohol and adheres to a plant-based diet, although he occasionally consumes processed foods during particularly stressful weeks.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Persistent difficulty initiating sleep; anxiety manageable with therapy and medication; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Stable headache frequency and intensity; no visual changes or neurological deficits. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Notable fatigue; no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 120/76 mmHg, HR 70 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert and oriented, appears fatigued but in no acute distress. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable but with noted fatigue.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 200 mg daily. Reinforce tapering of lorazepam use as needed. Schedule follow-up therapy sessions to further enhance coping strategies. 2. Insomnia: Continue trazodone at 50 mg; increase dosage to 75 mg at bedtime due to persistent sleep initiation difficulties. Continue melatonin at 10 mg; maintain CBT-I strategies and closely monitor sleep patterns. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Increase amitriptyline dosage to 40 mg nightly to enhance headache management. If headaches persist despite this adjustment, discuss the initiation of preventive therapy with topiramate at the next visit. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Continue to emphasize the importance of physical activity and mindfulness practices. Consider a referral to a nutritionist for dietary optimization. Explore advanced sleep hygiene techniques to further improve sleep quality.
Follow-up appointment scheduled for 2028-04-01 to evaluate ongoing symptoms, assess treatment effectiveness, and discuss further medication adjustments as necessary. Mr. Smith is advised to contact the office sooner if he experiences any worsening of symptoms or adverse effects from medications.
